summary: This document is a research prediction/claim report (P1) arguing that BPC-157's angiogenic phenotype is not mediated by orthosteric binding to VEGFR2 ECD, but rather through FBXO22–BACH1 intracellular signaling. It proposes specific SPR/ITC assays to falsify the popular vendor-claimed VEGFR2 ECD binding hypothesis and cites literature KD values for BPC-157–FBXO22 interaction (~100 nM). The document is at TRL 1–2: it is a hypothesis/prediction with supporting literature but no original experimental data.

content_blocks.title: Document Header and Status
content_blocks.content: Title: P1 — BPC-157 angiogenic phenotype is not orthosteric VEGFR2 ECD binding. Status: PREDICTION. Lane: peptides. Risk class: research-discussion. Novelty: assumption-kill. Method: propose-assay. Swarm ID: P1. Document path: reports/2026-09-25/P1.md.

content_blocks.title: Central Claim
content_blocks.content: BPC-157 does not bind human VEGFR2 ECD with tight affinity. SPR/ITC will miss a tight KD against VEGFR2 ECD while the same peptide retains ~100 nM KD to FBXO22. The popular orthosteric-VEGFR2 explanation of BPC-157's angiogenic phenotype is claimed to be false. Vendor and popular copy treat BPC-157 as a direct VEGFR2 binder (uncited Kd 50–200 nM), but phenotype papers activate the VEGFR2–Akt–eNOS axis without ever measuring ECD binding.

content_blocks.title: Proposed Mechanism (FBXO22–BACH1 Pathway)
content_blocks.content: Proposed alternative mechanism: BPC-157 engages FBXO22 via Pro3 (SPR KD ≈ 100 nM from Zhang literature); the BPC-157–FBXO22 complex blocks BACH1 ubiquitination → BACH1 protein rises → PDGFB/EGFR/FGF2/FGFR1-linked HUVEC proliferation and tube formation. Hsieh-class readouts (VEGFR2 upregulation, internalization, Akt–eNOS phosphorylation, tubes) are described as pathway consequences, not proof of orthosteric ECD occupancy. If FBXO22–BACH1 is primary, recombinant VEGFR2 ECD SPR/ITC should show no tight KD; scramble and P3A remain negative controls on FBXO22.

content_blocks.title: Prediction Variables Table
content_blocks.content:
Four prediction variables are defined:
1. BPC157_VEGFR2_ECD_KD | PREDICTION | SPR (Biacore) or ITC vs recombinant human VEGFR2 ECD; scramble and P3A controls | Threshold: no tight specific binding — KD > 10 µM or no saturable 1:1 fit at ≤10 µM; vendor 50–200 nM claim expected to fail.
2. BPC157_FBXO22_KD | LITERATURE | Zhang Biacore T200, FBXO22 on CM5, 1:1 fit | KD = 1.0×10⁻⁷ M (100 nM); scramble KD = 2.6×10⁻⁴ M.
3. P3A_FBXO22_KD | UNKNOWN | Zhang alanine scan; units unresolved | Do not use as numeric prior.
4. vendor_VEGFR2_Kd_50_200nM | UNKNOWN | Commercial/blog claims; PubMed 0 SPR/ITC hits | Not LITERATURE until a primary paper exists.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Citations
content_blocks.content:
Four key references cited:
1. PMID 27847966 / DOI 10.1007/s00109-016-1488-y (Hsieh 2017): VEGFR2 upregulation, internalization, Akt–eNOS, tube formation; no ECD SPR/KD measurement.
2. PMID 41606641 / PMC12947506 / DOI 10.1186/s12964-026-02694-6 (Zhang 2026): BPC-157–FBXO22 SPR KD = 1.0×10⁻⁷ M (100 nM); scramble KD = 2.6×10⁻⁴ M; BACH1 stabilization; notes VEGFR2 physical binding unresolved.
3. PMID 33051481 / DOI 10.1038/s41598-020-74022-y: Src–Cav-1–eNOS modulation downstream of VEGFR2 work; no ECD binding assay.
4. PMID 31911270 / DOI 10.1016/j.ebiom.2019.102617: Bach1 suppresses angiogenesis in prior models (sign conflict with Zhang's effector claim).

content_blocks.title: Proposed Assay Design and Falsification Criteria
content_blocks.content: Proposed assay: SPR (Biacore) or ITC against recombinant human VEGFR2 ECD (preference for Ig1–3 vs full ECD construct; buffer matching Hsieh HUVEC conditions). Controls: scramble peptide and P3A (Pro3 alanine mutant). Prediction threshold: KD > 10 µM or no saturable 1:1 fit at ≤10 µM peptide concentration. Refutation criterion: SPR or ITC of BPC-157 WT against recombinant human VEGFR2 ECD returns a specific KD ≤ 200 nM (vendor-claimed range) with scramble and P3A showing ≥10× weaker binding under the same buffer and surface density.

key_findings: Central prediction: BPC-157 does not bind VEGFR2 ECD with tight affinity (predicted KD > 10 µM by SPR/ITC); the vendor-claimed 50–200 nM KD is uncited and unsupported by any primary SPR/ITC publication.
Literature KD for BPC-157 binding to FBXO22: 1.0×10⁻⁷ M (100 nM) by Biacore T200 (Zhang 2026, PMID 41606641); scramble peptide KD = 2.6×10⁻⁴ M, confirming sequence specificity.

Proposed alternative mechanism: BPC-157 → FBXO22 engagement (via Pro3) → BACH1 ubiquitination blockade → BACH1 protein stabilization → PDGFB/EGFR/FGF2/FGFR1-driven HUVEC proliferation and angiogenesis.

Hsieh 2017 (PMID 27847966) demonstrated VEGFR2 upregulation, internalization, Akt–eNOS phosphorylation, and tube formation but performed no ECD binding assay (SPR/ITC), making orthosteric VEGFR2 binding unproven.
Zhang 2026 explicitly notes VEGFR2 physical binding is unresolved, supporting the prediction that ECD binding is absent.
Sign conflict identified: PMID 31911270 shows BACH1 suppresses angiogenesis in prior models, conflicting with Zhang's claim that BACH1 stabilization drives pro-angiogenic output.
No original experimental data are presented in this document; it is a hypothesis/prediction at TRL 1 proposing specific assays to test the claim.

Assay design recommendation: use Ig1–3 VEGFR2 ECD construct, buffer matching Hsieh HUVEC conditions, with scramble and P3A as negative controls; falsification threshold is KD ≤ 200 nM with ≥10× selectivity over controls.
